source_name: Southern Transitional Council (renamed Southern Arab Transitional Council, 2026), official site
selection_reason: Official platform of the main southern separatist organisation; publishes statements of its presidency, General Secretariat and local bodies, which remain central to the southern question despite the disputed January 2026 dissolution.
yemen_coverage: daily Homepage on 2026-10-04 carried a statement of an expanded extraordinary meeting of central and local bodies, a "presidential" message to southern forces and the emblem of a 14 October 2026 mobilisation event.
institutional_importance: high 2026 status, as the sources describe it: after the Saudi-backed campaign in Hadramawt and al-Mahra and the PLC takeover of Aden (2026-01-07), STC members in Riyadh led by secretary-general Ahmed Saeed bin Brik announced the council's dissolution on 2026-01-09 (Anadolu, Al Jazeera). The UAE-based spokesman Anwar al-Tamimi and members abroad rejected it as made under pressure and said the STC remained operational (Wikipedia). Chairman Aidarus al-Zubaidi left Aden on 2026-01-07 for Somaliland and then the UAE (Wikipedia) and was dismissed from the PLC. The council renamed itself the Southern Arab Transitional Council around April-May 2026 (Erem News), held a mass rally in Aden on 2026-05-04 (South24), and in September 2026 its foreign-affairs representative Amr al-Bidh spoke from Abu Dhabi, calling the dissolution coerced (Al-Monitor). It therefore operates as a contested, partly exiled organisation with activity still visible in Aden.
sub_alignment: Faction that rejected the January 2026 dissolution (al-Zubaidi, al-Tamimi, al-Bidh); not the Riyadh-based members who announced it
influence_components: yemen_coverage=25; indicators=1; reason=no citable audience figure
